text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Polluted parks get little help: Ottawa has no plan to clean up contaminated parks and heritage properties
-De Guzman family seeks tests on body: Print sets seem to differ, brother says -N.Korea on brink of famine, UN says:
-Hostel thrives in 'damp' environment: Seaton House Annex shelters men who would rather freeze than dry out

-Neighbourhood's pulse grows faint: Megacorporations are displacing local businesses on Ottawa's Elgin Street and long-time residents say the area's spirit is being destroyed. Third of an occasional series.
-UPS strike jolts business: Companies scramble as deliveries halted by walkout; firm says Canadian imnpact 'minimal'
-Novopharm scores ulcer drug coup: Deal with Genpharm puts generic version of Zantac on U.S. market a month before competitors
-Torstar hopes to write the book on selling educational products: Publisher says booming industry needs its marketing savvy
-Papua New Guinea's prince of privatization: Canadian David Beatty gets called first when the Pacific nation sells off its resources.
-Novopharm gets Zantac deal: Pact with rival will give Toronto drug maker a US$150M headstart marketing generic version of ulcer drug Zantac, one of the world's top-selling medicines
-Apple to unveil new weapon in its struggle to survive
